column11: derived: Bristol Myers generated $39,438mm of free cash flow on $141,500mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 27.87% margin, against the 30.0% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The smallest of these adjustments by some way: the filed lines nearly reconcile already, and the five-year aggregate of 28.5% says the window is not doing the work. Restated before interest: BMY paid $5,100mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 3.60% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 2.46% to 0.00%. Restated at replacement capex: BMY spent $3,768mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $1,883mm of plant depreciation, 1.33% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Restated without one-off cash: BMY's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $2,357mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 567mm; 2024 instalment 799mm; 2025 instalment 991mm). None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 BMY's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,026mm, inventories up $1,421mm, payables up $380mm, a working capital build of $2,067mm, 1.46% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at nil where the filed figures rebuild it at -4.68%, and stays there.

column12: Judgement on method: a 30-day fill is a days-supply unit, so capsule strength does not enter it, which matters here because the label's 160 mg dose is given as 40 mg or 160 mg capsules. column11: already approved in this population, so the layer adds nothing. Section 1.1 of the Augtyro label (DailyMed set id fb526827-40ba-4462-94cf-179ae3b0cb8a, spl version 6, effective 2026-08-11, the row the book's labels table carries) states that 'AUGTYRO is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)', with no restriction on prior therapy, and this is a full approval rather than the accelerated one section 1.2 carries for NTRK fusion solid tumours. TRIDENT-3 (NCT06140836) enrols inside it: 'histologically or cytologically confirmed diagnosis of locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC', 'a ROS1 gene rearrangement/fusion as detected by a local test', 'must not be exposed previously with TKIs that demonstrated activities in ROS1-positive NSCLC' and 'Up to 1 prior line of systemic treatment for NSCLC is permitted'. Section 14.1 of the same label shows the approval already rested on that population: 'The efficacy populations included 71 ROS1 TKI-naive patients who received up to 1 prior line of platinum-based chemotherapy and/or immunotherapy'. The book's Enhertu row for this indication carries 1.0 for the same situation
column12: the readout moves evidence and share of regimen, not patients. TRIDENT-3 is the randomised comparison against crizotinib that TRIDENT-1's single arm could not give, so it defends first-line use rather than opening a population the label does not already reach. No pool, eligibility, penetration or ramp row is written: indication_layer.build returns early on an overlap of 1.0 and asks for none
